title: Physical meaning of gradient and area
keyIdea: The gradient of a graph is a rate (speed, acceleration, power); the area under a graph is an accumulated amount (distance, energy).

kid: A graph's steepness shows a rate. On a distance–time graph, steep means fast.
The area under some graphs shows a total. On a speed–time graph, the area is the distance. Always check the units on the axes to see what the gradient and the area mean.
adult: To read a gradient, divide the y units by the x units. On a distance–time graph, m ÷ s gives speed. On a velocity–time graph you get acceleration. On an energy–time graph, J ÷ s is power in watts.
To read an area, multiply the units. Velocity × time gives distance, and power × time gives energy. If the units multiply to nothing useful, the area has no real meaning.

familyTip: Pick any graph in a news story. Ask: what would its gradient mean? Does its area mean anything?
